source_text: His itaque tu dissertionibus, cervino metu, et vulpino dolo obviam ire conatus, ita imposuisti patrono tuo ad quem scribis, ut referres, propter sensum corporis naturalem, id est concupiscentiam carnis, dominari operibus et imagini Dei principem tenebrarum; cum necesse esset ad eumdem spectare auctorem sensum carnis, ad quem etiam carnis natura respiceret.
pass_a_gloss: By these dissertations therefore you, having tried to go against them with stag-like fear and fox-like deceit, so imposed on your patron to whom you write, that you reported that on account of the natural sense of the body, that is the desire of the flesh, the prince of darkness rules the works and the image of God; when it was necessary that the sense of the flesh look to the same author to whom also the nature of the flesh looks.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: Trying to meet these arguments with a deer’s fear and a fox’s deceit, you deceived the patron to whom you write by telling him that the ruler of darkness dominates God’s works and image because of natural bodily sensation, that is, the desire of the flesh (compare Genesis 1:26–27). Yet the flesh’s sensation must necessarily belong to the same author as the flesh’s nature.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
